name: Can pool demolition be approved if the yard will be regraded afterward?

mainEntity.name: Can pool demolition be approved if the yard will be regraded afterward, and does that change the permit scope?
mainEntity.text: Can pool demolition be approved if the yard will be regraded afterward, and does that change the permit scope?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regrading after pool demolition often changes the project from a straightforward teardown into a site restoration job. Once the contractor starts changing slopes, drainage patterns, or finished yard elevations, the city may require a broader permit scope and more documentation. That can include grading plans, drainage notes, or a soils report if the area will support future use. Homeowners should mention any intended regrading at the start because it affects permitting, inspection sequence, and fill methods. The city is concerned about where water will go after the pool is gone and whether the ground will settle later. A clear plan for the final yard shape can prevent surprise permit revisions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but regrading can change the scope from simple demolition to a more involved grading or site work permit. The city may want more detailed plans, drainage information, and compaction requirements before approval.
